column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline rule actions for the AutoPWN Suite dashboard.
#   or:   <rule id><TAB>OUTOFSCOPE<TAB><URL regex>  (drops that rule's alerts for matching URLs only)
# status as a failed gate: FAIL (exit 1) and every rule that is not listed here
# (reported as WARN, exit 2, i.e. "not triaged yet") both block the release.
# Only IGNORE/OUTOFSCOPE entries below pass, and each one carries a written justification.
# Rules that ZAP reports as PASS need no entry.
# Triaged against real scans of the unauthenticated surface (login page and
# redirects) and an authenticated pass (dashboard, static assets, API GETs).
# Re-triaged after the dashboard added CSP, Permissions-Policy, COOP/COEP/CORP headers
# and a POST login form; a headless Firefox confirmed the dashboard still loads under them.
# --- Hardening rules that now PASS: kept as FAIL so a regression blocks the release ---

column3: Content-Security-Policy must be present on every response
COEP/COOP/CORP cross-origin isolation headers must be present
No credentials or other sensitive data in URLs; the sign-in form now uses method=post

column1: # --- Open true finding: do not ignore until fixed ---

column3: Server header still discloses Werkzeug/Python versions (Low, true finding): the response header set in after_request is sent in addition to the development server's own Server header, so two Server headers are emitted; override the server's version string instead

column1: # --- Informational or false positives, each justified ---

column3: CSP unsafe-inline (script-src and style-src): accepted for now because modules/web_ui_static/index.html still has inline on* event handlers and style attributes that need it; the sign-in page (/login, /login.js, /login.css) keeps a strict policy with no unsafe-inline, and everything else is limited to same-origin with object-src 'none', base-uri 'none' and frame-ancestors 'none'. Remove this entry when the inline handlers are moved into app.js so the dashboard policy can be tightened

column1: # 10202 (Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens) is scoped out only for the sign-in form served at / and /login: it is a no-script fallback that targets POST /login, which accepts only GET (405), so it changes no state. The real sign-in is a fetch POST to /api/auth/login that requires the X-CSRF-Token header bound to a challenge cookie, with SameSite=Strict cookies and an Origin check. Caveat: the URL scope cannot tell the sign-in page from the authenticated dashboard at /, so a future token-less HTML form on the dashboard page would not be reported; every other URL is still gated (an unlisted 10202 alert is a WARN)

column3: Private IP Disclosure: false positive; 192.168.1.0 and 10.0.0.1 are example CIDR/target placeholders in the scan form and in web_security.js, not leaked addresses
Suspicious Comments: false positive; the matched word is "user" in ordinary explanatory comments in app.js and web_security.js
Non-Storable Content: intentional; every dashboard response sends Cache-Control: no-store because responses are private and per-session
Modern Web Application: informational notice that the page is script-driven; not a vulnerability
Authentication Request Identified: informational detection of the login form; not a vulnerability
